source.title: Wave-like dopamine dynamics as a mechanism for spatiotemporal credit assignment.

confidence_rationale: Shows striatal dopamine is NOT one uniform broadcast: it travels as waves organised by functional subregion, with direction set by task agency, and the authors propose this as a credit-assignment mechanism. Supports the claim's goal (credit must land on the right loop) but undercuts its premise (a single shared delta_t with all locality in the trace). Evidence class: in vivo widefield imaging of dopamine axons and release.
failure_signatures: Dopamine release organises into localised, subregion-specific clusters and travelling waves, contradicting the premise that the teaching signal is a single globally uniform broadcast.

The proposed credit-assignment mechanism acts through the spatial structure of the dopamine SIGNAL itself, an alternative to (or complement of) purely trace-based locality; if it is the dominant mechanism, loop-local traces under a uniform delta_t would be an incomplete model.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Dopamine axon activity and release across dorsal striatum form wave-like spatiotemporal patterns that cluster transients within functionally related subregions; wave direction is tailored to task demands (dorsomedial to dorsolateral when reward depends on behaviour, the opposite when it does not), proposed as a mechanism directing credit assignment to specialised striatal subregions.
mapping.ree_translation: Bears on MECH-452's premise rather than its conclusion. MECH-452 assumes one shared delta_t and puts all loop-specificity into the eligibility term; Hamid et al. suggest the brain ALSO localises credit by shaping the dopamine signal per region (a DMS/associative vs DLS/motor gradient that maps loosely onto REE's associative vs motor loops). The claim's end state -- credit landing on the loop that acted -- is supported; its mechanism, 'global signal x local trace', may be only half the story.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rodent widefield imaging of axons and release; the link from wave direction to credit assignment is a proposed computational account with supporting correlations, not a causal demonstration. REE could represent this either by loop-specific delta_t (contradicting the 'single signal' framing) or by treating waves as a gain on local traces (compatible).
mapping.source_context: Mice, widefield imaging of dopamine axon activity and dopamine release across dorsal striatum during instrumental and Pavlovian tasks; computational model of agency-dependent wave dynamics.

confidence_components.notes: High-impact study; direction mixed because it supports localised credit while challenging the uniform-broadcast premise.
